summary: Julius Müller was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Breslau, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held posts at Göttingen (~1830–1835), Marburg (~1835–1839), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1839–1878).
Julius Pokorny worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Vienna under Rudolf Much (~1905–1908). He held positions at Vienna, Berlin, Bern, Zurich, Kiel, Munich, and Erlangen-Nuremberg.
Julius Schubring studied at the University of Bonn (~1857–1858), the University of Göttingen (~1858–1860), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1860–1862).

Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a doctorate in literature at the University of Tokyo. He served as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2009 to 2013.

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology, religious studies, and computational fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, and held posts at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science, Aichi Prefectural University, Toyo University, and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Jun Yang is a sinology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2026, affiliations are attested as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Language at the University of Chicago and commissioned researcher at Koyasan University.

Jundo Nagashima studied Indology and Buddhist studies under Seitatsu Matsunami, Alexis Sanderson, and Paul Williams, earning a PhD from the University of Bristol. Nagashima held posts at Taisho University, attested between 2006 and 2017.

June McDaniel is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS from Emory University and a Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. She held posts in philosophy, religion, and religious studies at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

Junglan Bang specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Dongguk University and under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn before completing a PhD at Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson (2012). Bang served as a visiting researcher at Kyoto University.

Jungmin Ha works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Ha completed a master's at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a Doctor of Philosophy from Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016).

Junjiro Takakusu, a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar, studied at Ryukoku, Oxford, Berlin, and Leipzig under Friedrich Max Müller, Sylvain Lévi, and Moriz Winternitz. He held leadership roles and professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University.

Junkei Washio, active in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, studied at Toyo University (~1889–1892). He held posts at Sendan-Rin School and as professor at Komazawa University and Toyo University.

Junkichi Imanishi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Ernst Waldschmidt. He held posts at Hokkaido University, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Junko Matsumura is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned an MA at the Australian National University and completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen. Matsumura held a professorship at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).

Junko Minamoto is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who completed a master's at Ryukoku University and doctoral coursework at Otani University. Minamoto held a post as a commissioned researcher at Kansai University.
Junko Sakamoto-Gotō is an Indologist and linguist with attested affiliations at Tohoku University (2005) and Ryukoku University (2015).

Junsho Kato is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tokyo, KU Leuven, and under Étienne Lamotte, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura. He held professorships at Nishogakusha University (1972) and Nagoya University (~1982–2003).
Junzo Inagaki studied Buddhist studies under Shoshin Fukihara and held a post as section chief at Otani University.
Juri Lotman was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy who completed his studies at Saint Petersburg State University and held a post at the University of Tartu in 1954.
Juro Watanabe studied Indology and philosophy under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested between 1989 and 1990.
